plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you never overpay since you only pay the second-highest bid, and bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies. Bidding below value risks losing profitable auctions; bidding above value risks negative profit. With value $25, the optimal bid is exactly $25.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding below value only risks losing profitable auctions, while bidding above value risks negative profit. With a value of $3, bidding exactly $3 ensures I only win when profitable (paying less than $3) and never lose money.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that second-highest bid, never overpaying. Shading down doesn't help since payment depends on others' bids, not mine. Bidding above value risks losses if I win at a price above my value. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $26 to maximize expected profit.
